Steps.1: Check on the datasheet of the ESD protecting diodes (D3 & D4) if the clamping voltage (V_CL) is less than 45V and have bidirectional ESD protection.
Steps.2: Connect the hw_DAA to a PC. Execute the CAN test to verify its performance.
Steps.3: Check the output log file from the test, to verify the good functionality of the CAN transceivers at the beginning of the test.
Steps.4: Place the hw_DAA on the isolator of the ESD table.
Steps.5: Connect the hw_DAA to a DAA CS harness.
Steps.6: Connect a GND signal of the DAA CS harness (through a crocodile clip) to the ground plane.
Steps.7: Connect the power transformer isolator to the power supply source.
Steps.8: Connect the power supply source with some bananas to the back of the LISN.
Steps.9: Connect the LISN with some bananas to the DC power connector.
Steps.10: Switch on the power supply source.
Steps.11: Set 12V and 3A on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.12: Turn on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.13: Configure the ESD generator with an air discharge tip.
Steps.14: Connect the ESD simulator to the ground of the installation.
Steps.15: Connect the horizontal coupling plane to the ground reference plane using a cable with 2x470 KOhms.
Steps.17: Configure on the ESD simulator to create positive and negative polarities pulses of 15000 Volts following the IT.736 - ESD Dito System.
Steps.18: Charge the ESD generator and approach a selected CAN signals at a speed used for a human hand reaching towards an object (~0.3 m/s) until the generator discharges or contact is made with the test point. After discharge or contact occurs, the discharge electrode shall be removed from the signal. Recharge for another discharge.
Steps.19: Repeat step 18 for all the CAN signals.
Steps.20: Connect again the hw_DAA to a PC. Execute the CAN test to verify its performance.
Steps.21: Check the output log file from the test, to verify the good functionality of the CAN transceivers after the application of the pulses.
